source_refs.note: Topic 23.4.1 with Quick Check 23.3, answered (PDF 108-110); the methods are summarised in an original figure. 'propanol' in the Quick Check is read as propan-1-ol. Answers need review.

items: Oxidation of primary alcohols and aldehydes: the starting material is heated under reflux with excess acidified KMnO4 or K2Cr2O7: CH3CH2OH + 2[O] -> CH3COOH + H2O; CH3CHO + [O] -> CH3COOH.

Hydrolysis of nitriles: in acid, nitriles give carboxylic acids directly, CH3CN + 2H2O + HCl -> CH3COOH + NH4Cl; in alkali they first give the salt, CH3CN + H2O + NaOH -> CH3COONa + NH3, which gives the acid on acidification, CH3COONa + HCl -> CH3COOH + NaCl.

Hydrolysis of esters: refluxing with dilute acid gives the acid and the alcohol, CH3COOCH2CH3 + H2O <=> CH3COOH + CH3CH2OH (H3O+); with dilute alkali the carboxylate salt forms, CH3COOCH2CH3 + NaOH -> CH3COONa + CH3CH2OH, and acidifying gives the acid.
Benzoic acid (benzenecarboxylic acid): methylbenzene is readily oxidised by acidified KMnO4 or K2Cr2O7: C6H5CH3 + 3[O] -> C6H5COOH + H2O (KMnO4, dilute H2SO4, heat).

blocks.alt: Four boxes with arrows to R-COOH: oxidation, CH3CH2OH + 2[O] -> CH3COOH + H2O with K2Cr2O7/dilute H2SO4 under reflux; nitrile hydrolysis, CH3CN + 2H2O + HCl -> CH3COOH + NH4Cl, or NaOH then acid; ester hydrolysis, CH3COOC2H5 + H2O <=> CH3COOH + C2H5OH; side-chain oxidation, C6H5CH3 + 3[O] -> C6H5COOH + H2O with KMnO4.
blocks.caption: Four ways of making carboxylic acids (original summary of the book's methods).
blocks.long_description: Carboxylic acids are made by oxidation (of primary alcohols, aldehydes or the side chain of an alkylbenzene) or by hydrolysis (of nitriles or esters). After an alkaline hydrolysis the acid is present as its salt and must be released by adding a stronger acid.

blocks.prompt: Write the equation for the oxidation of propan-1-ol with acidified K2Cr2O7 (under reflux).
blocks.explanation: CH3CH2CH2OH + 2[O] -> CH3CH2COOH + H2O (propanoic acid; propanal is formed first).

blocks.prompt: Give the products and equations for (i) hydrolysis of CH3CH2CN, (ii) oxidation of ethylbenzene, (iii) hydrolysis of ethyl ethanoate.
blocks.explanation: (i) CH3CH2CN + 2H2O + HCl -> CH3CH2COOH + NH4Cl (propanoic acid). (ii) C6H5CH2CH3 + 6[O] -> C6H5COOH + CO2 + 2H2O (benzoic acid; KMnO4, heat). (iii) CH3COOCH2CH3 + H2O <=> CH3COOH + CH3CH2OH (ethanoic acid and ethanol).

items: Oxidise primary alcohols or aldehydes (reflux, acidified dichromate).
Hydrolyse nitriles or esters (alkali, then acidify).
